title: Decoding the Decoder LLM without de code: Ishan Anand
talk_summary: A pedagogical walkthrough of GPT-2 small implemented entirely in an Excel spreadsheet, covering tokenization, embeddings, attention, MLP, residual stream, logit lens, and sparse-autoencoder activation steering.

takeaways.what_they_do: They note that RWKV's pseudo-attention cannot look backward like a Transformer, so its official prompt template swaps the usual order of instructions and context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they recommend you swap the traditional order of instructions and context because the attention mechanism ... can't look back the same way

takeaways.what_they_do: They attach the language head between every layer to see what the model would predict at each depth, revealing when the correct answer appears, vanishes, and is re-promoted.

takeaways.technique: Activation steering via sparse autoencoder features
takeaways.what_they_do: They extract an interpretable feature direction (e.g. 'Jedi') from a sparse autoencoder, scale it, and add it into the residual stream to bias generation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I've basically multiply it by a coefficient and then I've basically formatted it so that I can inject it right into the residual stream
